rulings.barItem: a refusal without a cause the story shows, or the same cause drawn twice; a run of refusals
rulings.reason: Act 2 refuses 'a key never issued by this World', act 5 refuses 'a URL without a published blob', act 6 refuses text= given twice and act 7 keeps 'an unpublished CSS representation' as a refused gap, but no actor in the story sends any of these: the pinned helper always sends the World's issued key (demand.json, fetchGoogleFonts.ts:62) and downloads only URLs Google's CSS returned, Dub sends no text= and Rallly sends one (https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/css2: "the 'text=' parameter can only be specified once", so nobody here sends two). Together with act 6's other refusals they make a closing run of refusals.
rulings.correction: Remove these four refusals from acts 2, 5, 6 and 7; keep a refusal only where an actor in the story has a reason to send that request.

rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: Act 6 says a browser asking CSS2 and Rallly's CJK text subset 'are refused'. Google documents text= for exactly this case: "This feature also works for international fonts, allowing you to specify UTF-8 characters" (https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/css2, https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/getting_started). It also documents the stylesheet link as something placed in an HTML document for the browser to fetch (getting_started: 'add a special stylesheet link to your HTML document'). Google answers both requests with a stylesheet, and Rallly, named in the outline's title, is left with no successful call.
rulings.correction: In act 6, have Rallly's Noto Sans SC wght@700 text= request answered with Google's retained CSS2 response and its truetype file (published in act 1), or take Rallly out of the title and story. Drop the browser refusal.

rulings.barItem: a read-back with no need: a list or get of what the story already holds, unless someone who does not hold it reads it
rulings.reason: In act 2 the World asks for the key it was just issued again in the same sitting, before any resume. In act 6 the same CSS2 stylesheet is read a second time under a second server agent ('the same for node and undici'), but Dub is the only CSS2 caller and already holds it. That the two agents get the same answer is evidence for vendor/inter.json, not an act of anyone in the story.
rulings.correction: Move the repeated key read into act 7's resume, where a re-booted World genuinely asks again, and drop the undici comparison from act 6.
